subject: Urban Planning
subcategory: Parks, Green Spaces, and Public Land
title: Permeable Pavement: Letting Water Through
description: A micro-lesson that makes Permeable Pavement: Letting Water Through usable.

hook.text: Traditional pavement sends every raindrop into storm drains. Permeable pavement lets water soak straight through.

buildup.text: Porous asphalt, permeable concrete, and interlocking pavers filter rainwater into the ground beneath them.

discovery.text: A permeable parking lot can eliminate 70-80% of stormwater runoff, reducing flooding and sewer overflow.

twist.text: Permeable surfaces cost 10-15% more upfront but eliminate the need for separate drainage infrastructure.

climax.text: Chicago installed permeable alleys citywide. Flooding complaints in treated areas dropped dramatically.

punchline.text: Let the parking lot drink the rain. The sewer says thanks.

quiz.question: How much stormwater runoff can permeable pavement eliminate?
